model_annotations.Bulgarian:
Figure 6 compares the distribution of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five different gating configurations in a neural network model. The horizontal axis, labeled "Layer," represents the layer number within the model, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, marked at intervals of 5. The vertical axis, labeled "Max," represents the maximum activation value, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400, marked at intervals of 100. The figure contains five distinct plots, each corresponding to a different gating configuration.

The first plot, labeled "Row 1 (Baseline)," shows a single line in red. This line starts at a value of 0 at Layer 0, rises sharply to a peak of approximately 400 at Layer 6, and then decreases to a value of about 200 at Layer 20. The second plot, labeled "Row 2 (SDPA Gating)," shows a single line in green. This line starts at a value of 0 at Layer 0, remains low until Layer 6, and then increases to a value of approximately 200 at Layer 20. The third plot, labeled "Row 3 (Value Layer Gating)," shows a single line in blue. This line starts at a value of 0 at Layer 0, rises sharply to a peak of approximately 400 at Layer 6, and then decreases to a value of about 200 at Layer 20. The fourth plot, labeled "Row 4 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid)," shows a single line in purple. This line starts at a value of 0 at Layer 0, rises sharply to a peak of approximately 400 at Layer 6, and then decreases to a value of about 200 at Layer 20. The fifth plot, labeled "Row 5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid)," shows a single line in black. This line starts at a value of 0 at Layer 0, rises sharply to a peak of approximately 400 at Layer 6, and then decreases to a value of about 200 at Layer 20.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 6 compares the distribution of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a neural network. The x-axis represents the network layer, ranging from 0 to 22 in linear scale with a step of 1, while the y-axis shows the magnitude of activations or attention sink values, scaled from 0 to 400 for the left plot and 0 to 0.2 for the right plot. The left plot displays four lines: a red line with circular markers that peaks sharply at layer 6 with a value of approximately 400 and then decreases; a green line with triangular markers that rises gradually, peaks at layer 18 with a value around 200, and then declines; a black line with square markers that remains low and flat across all layers; and a blue line with diamond markers that stays near zero until layer 10, after which it rises steadily to a value of about 200 at layer 22. The right plot shows a single blue line with diamond markers that remains near zero until layer 10, then increases sharply to a value of approximately 0.2 by layer 22.
model_annotations.English: Figure 6 compares the massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations. Row 1 (Baseline): Significant massive activations and attention sinks emerge after the 6th layer. Row 2 (SDPA Gating): Reduced activations and no attention sinks observed. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating): Similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid): Massive activations and attention sinks resemble the baseline.
model_annotations.German: Figure 6 compares the distribution of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a neural network. The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 24 in integer steps, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Mass" and spans from 0 to 400, with major tick marks at intervals of 100. The first subplot displays four lines: a red solid line that starts at 0, rises sharply to approximately 400 at layer 6, then decreases to around 100 at layer 10, and increases again to about 350 at layer 24; a green dashed line that begins at 0, remains near 0 until layer 10, then rises to approximately 150 at layer 24; a blue dotted line that stays close to 0 across all layers; and a black dash-dotted line that remains flat near 0. The second subplot shows a single blue solid line that starts at 0, remains near 0 until layer 10, then increases sharply to about 2.5 at layer 24.
